stem: During active-shooter preparedness training, which response sequence should the nurse identify as consistent with CISA guidance?

options.A: Confront the attacker first, then decide whether to hide or evacuate.
options.B: Remain in place in every situation even when a safe escape route exists.
options.C: Wait for law enforcement before taking any protective action.
options.D: Run if a safe escape is possible; if not, hide; fight only as a last resort.

rationale: CISA active-shooter guidance uses the Run, Hide, Fight framework: evacuate when possible, hide when evacuation is not possible, and fight only as a last resort when life is in imminent danger.
educational_objective: Recall the CISA Run-Hide-Fight sequence for active-shooter response.
source_locator: Active Shooter Preparedness — Run, Hide, Fight; Fight as a last resort
source_claim_supported: CISA recommends Run if possible, Hide if evacuation is not possible, and Fight only as a last resort.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — emergency preparedness
correction_summary: Aligned the item with the current CISA Run-Hide-Fight framework and removed nonstandard response sequences.
